behavior: Run state table: planning, working, waiting, blocked, failed, completed, cancelled (incl. canceled/canceling/skipped), derived from tracked work; batch titles come from the work; upkeep is detected.
given_when_then: Given convoy data, when derived, then run state.

behavior: Agent state table: working, idle, waiting, blocked, stopped, crashed; a running session outranks a stopped word and is the live truth; agents join sessions, unclaimed sessions become agents, only live agents are listed and suspended ones kept while slots dropped.
given_when_then: Given agent and session facts, when derived, then one state.

behavior: Gates come from choices, confirmations, free text, gate beads, failed runs and review-ready, and mapGates collects every source.
given_when_then: Given sources, when mapped, then one gate each.

behavior: Gate rows and capabilities render for the team, and gate notifications give one alert per gate (baseline first, per id and kind), fixed copy with ids only, dismissed on settle, and nothing posted in the foreground.
given_when_then: Given new gates, when app is background, then one alert each; foreground none.

behavior: The team glance counts working and needs-you (needs-you first, at most three) and shows idle when nothing is open.
given_when_then: Given tasks, when summarised, then glance ordered.

behavior: The host guide's address hint names the port the guide starts the front on.
given_when_then: Given the guide, when shown, then port matches.

behavior: Merge gate: presence, approve, merge, receipt states and review changes behave per spec; MergeReadiness decodes leniently; merge requests round-trip and confirm on events; nothing destructive (force, reset, delete) exists on the phone in verbs, keys or copy.
given_when_then: Given merge flow, when used, then safe and confirmed.

behavior: A wrong folder and a rejected sign-in during team models setup read in plain words.
given_when_then: Given setup errors, when shown, then plain wording.

behavior: Every team state value (work, run, agent, gate, product) has an unknown member, and garbage provider strings map to unknown instead of failing.
given_when_then: Given an unrecognised provider string, when mapped, then the result is unknown and nothing throws.

behavior: Gas City bead, agent, session, run, run-kind and gate-kind strings map to the documented states per the work/agent tables.
given_when_then: Given each provider status string, when mapped, then it yields the table's state.

behavior: A work item's displayed state is derived from its facts by a fixed precedence order.
given_when_then: Given combinations of bead, run, gate and agent facts, when state is derived, then the highest-precedence state wins.

behavior: Every team model keeps the raw provider payload and raw state alongside the mapped fields.
given_when_then: Given a provider object, when parsed, then raw data and raw state are retained.

behavior: Every team event type carries a sequence number, raw payload and type, the set of event types is closed so handling is exhaustive, and an event cursor supports resuming from a point.
given_when_then: Given any event, when read, then seq, raw and type exist; given a cursor, when resumed, then reading continues after it.

behavior: Team capability sets are consistent: none is all off, the fixture is all on, the front-end set is read plus exactly the control switches, the phone-loopback set is read plus controls, and the read set covers what the spike proved.
given_when_then: Given each capability constant, when compared, then the stated relations hold and every field in the architecture plan is present.

behavior: With no team backend, reads return empty results, the event stream ends immediately, and every control answers a rejected receipt carrying the request id; closing is harmless.
given_when_then: Given the null gateway, when read, controlled or closed, then nothing throws and controls are rejected with their id.

behavior: A mutation receipt has four outcomes and host identity compares by value.
given_when_then: Given two identical host identities, when compared, then they are equal.

behavior: Agent output merges cumulative, overlapping and new chunks without duplication, and an agent transcript is parsed from markers, repeats and prose.
given_when_then: Given overlapping output chunks, when merged, then text is not repeated.

behavior: The team layer is plain logic: it must not depend on UI or on the protocol clients directly.
given_when_then: DROPPED-adjacent architecture rule kept as note.

behavior: The team's now-line tells honestly what is happening: a 31-minute planning shows an honest reason with a way out that does not resend, stalls and unavailable connections give next steps and recovery, estimates are optional, a question takes priority, and finished outcomes stay distinct without cancel or timing.
given_when_then: Given run facts, when the line is built, then reason, next step and recovery match the state.

behavior: Asleep is not paused; a waiting task says when a worker starts; the agent screen and live output never spin forever; the in-app team checks every minute.
given_when_then: Given a sleeping team, when shown, then it reads asleep not paused; given no output, then no endless spinner.

behavior: Team overview: session evidence wins while waiting and blocked stay explicit; idle is not paused; missing, stale or unknown evidence stays unknown; a heat pause needs a matching profile, phone host and city.
given_when_then: Given partial evidence, when summarized, then unknown is never shown as a known state.

behavior: The team page shows one page whether the plugin is on or off, what the team spent today, how it runs, and says what to check when the host does not answer.
given_when_then: Given the team on or off, when the page opens, then state and spend are shown plainly.

behavior: Team discovery and setup rows: a first unreachable answer reads as Checking not failure, demo mode reads Demo never On, read-only and unreachable states are named, manual add and host kinds work, turning off is explicit, discovery URLs follow the tailnet rule, a dismissal expires after 30 days, and the found host is shared with sibling screens.
given_when_then: Given a first unreachable probe, when shown, then Checking; given a dismissal older than 30 days, then discovery offers again.

behavior: Team policy: the front policy document decodes leniently, unknown or missing supervision is balanced, the policy route handles with and without rig and answers 404 and 422, the policy is cached with project scope and kept when a refresh fails, and is absent when the gateway has no policy side.
given_when_then: Given a failing policy read, when refreshed, then the previous policy stays and is marked stale.

behavior: Engine refusals survive as typed codes through a thrown failure, while untyped failures stay generic and never retain secrets; an accepted command stays accepted when its refresh fails; late polls or reads never replace newer data.
given_when_then: Given a late poll after a newer refresh, when it arrives, then the newer snapshot stays.

behavior: Team editor lists roles and reads models by family, newest version first.
given_when_then: Given models of one family, when listed, then newest version is first.

behavior: Team project lifecycle: minor-only findings are left for the person; every-step merge needs confirmation and risky phase review guards main; interrupted work cannot move without a shared remote; a malformed plan can retry or become one reviewed task; manual commits survive and conflicts stop only their queue item; agent conflict resolution is a checked task on the original branch; the full lifecycle checks, fixes, rechecks, merges and confirms exact commits.
given_when_then: Given a plan run to completion, when merged, then exact commits are confirmed and main is guarded.

behavior: Team budget and planning rules: a budget warning appears once per day before the cap, the gate survives a cap with no running tasks, mode and budget are required before creating work, confirmed placement starts over instead of inventing a handoff, lane and dependency caps hold and cycles are rejected, quick tasks honor plan-first and the chosen role and server, replan cannot inject completed state.
given_when_then: Given a spend near the cap, when checked, then one warning per day; given a dependency cycle, then it is rejected.

behavior: Team project persistence: restart keeps the approved spec and receipts and interrupts live work, commands persist before publishing and stale or reused commands are rejected, delete drains in-flight writes without resurrection, and a read-only view never seeds or reconciles stored work.
given_when_then: Given a restart with live work, when reloaded, then spec stays and live work is marked interrupted.

behavior: The built-in team demo loads without recordings or a server, stopping and removing waits for closure and never starts a late simulator, and profile deletion closes the simulator before sweeping its records.
given_when_then: Given stop during loading, when it finishes, then no simulator starts later.

behavior: Planner state is additive: a server diagnostic reason does not change online, old project snapshots without planner data still load, planner gates and the timeline round-trip, and checkpoint updates keep workflow and revision.
given_when_then: Given a legacy snapshot, when read, then it loads with defaults.

behavior: Team refusal codes read plainly; unknown codes name the action to take.
given_when_then: Given a known or unknown refusal code, when shown, then plain words appear and no raw code is the only text.

behavior: The in-app team runtime status parses download failures, every phase and failure reason, and killed-by-Android with readiness; the runtime is supported only on 64-bit phones with pinned builds; verbs dispatch, poll status until idle and answer the last result; a refused dispatch is a bridge error; log tail and managed projects work; the download size is the pinned archives plus packages; the phone config is Gas City on loopback with this phone as host.
given_when_then: Given a setup verb, when dispatched, then status is polled to idle and the final answer returned.

behavior: Joined agent session state and running flag are carried to agents and to pool sessions with no agent entry; an agent with no session has neither; worker start stage comes from the reported session, only plausible starts are measured, and the last start is kept per profile.
given_when_then: Given an agent without a session, when mapped, then no state or running flag.

behavior: Status words stay honest: a spec taking minutes shows how long then says still working, and finished tasks never read as 0 working.
given_when_then: Given all tasks finished, when summarized, then no 0 working appears.

behavior: Task header line says who is on which step and since when and what is next, hides the step that is the task itself and times under a minute, says Next: merge only where a merge gate follows, shows where a waiting merge gate is without time, says how long ago a finished task ended, keeps host words for a question or problem, and defers to the line below when a wait is past its usual time.
given_when_then: Given a working task, when headed, then worker, step and elapsed are shown.

behavior: Usage evidence never invents numbers: partial and unpriced estimates are retained, unavailable or absent usage never becomes zero cost, recent sessions stay separate window snapshots not task totals, invalid figures are unknown, and future sources stay estimates.
given_when_then: Given absent usage, when shown, then unknown not zero.

behavior: Usage label: null when neither cost nor tokens reported, tokens written compactly, every cost carries est., cost and tokens join or appear alone, and Arabic keeps Latin figures and the suffix after the amount; task details say when a cost is unreported.
given_when_then: Given 12400 tokens and a cost, when labeled, then compact tokens plus est. cost.

behavior: The work graph lays out nodes deterministically, names and thickens the critical path, picks out the blocked chain (stuck item, its open need, its waiters), tolerates unknown ids, self links, duplicates and cycles, and scales with chip size; turning the plugin off sweeps the remembered view.
given_when_then: Given the same six-node graph, when laid out twice, then identical rectangles.

behavior: Codex account usage reads 5-hour and weekly limits and hashes the email; an API-key account is a key sign-in not a plan; signed-out is listed only if needed or used; a failing session is a broken reader and a dropped link offline; with no Codex connection nothing is read.
given_when_then: Given Codex responses, when read, then correct readings.

behavior: Paseo usage: opted-in servers and the phone host feed readings, automatic reading needs no switch, signed-out Claude Code becomes not-signed-in, and a stopped phone host is unreached and never started.
given_when_then: Given servers, when read, then readings per rules.

behavior: The collector source reads In-app Ubuntu for every provider and remote ones only with consent; unreachable remote is offline; expired sign-in is auth required; provider rate limit is a problem not error; alerts enrol In-app readings with no step and never auto-enrol remote collectors, nothing when alerts off.
given_when_then: Given collector states, when read, then statuses and enrolment.

behavior: API keys are not plan cards unless a plan reading exists; Claude via phone host or PC is one card each; signed-out Claude Code offers Sign in on the phone; Claude on OpenCode is a Details row; Paseo needing sign-in is still a Claude card; unreadable providers are not plan cards while Copilot via Paseo is.
given_when_then: Given provider kinds, when mapped, then card or not.

behavior: Every agent launch that sets the Claude config directory also sets the Claude home to match.
given_when_then: Given agent launch env, when built, then both set.

behavior: Widget steering uses steer delivery where supported; unsupported steering falls back to an after-reply send; unknown mixed runtime never sends a prompt; an uncertain send is not replayed and never exposes remote text.
given_when_then: Given capability, when widget sends, then correct delivery or none

behavior: Worktree inspection reports exact copy changes, keeping an error as unknown rather than clean; conversation membership uses exact project, path and workspace; empty matching pages keep continuation and failures propagate; unsupported or invalid scopes dispatch no requests.
given_when_then: Given worktree, when inspected, then exact state or unknown

behavior: The ACP handshake works when bytes arrive fragmented mid-UTF8 character, keeps unknown additions, and exposes only safe capabilities.
given_when_then: Given a fragmented handshake reply, when parsed, then capabilities are intact and unknown fields are tolerated

behavior: An unsupported negotiated protocol version closes the ACP connection.
given_when_then: Given server version unsupported, when initialize completes, then client closes

behavior: A session cannot be created before initialization and requires an absolute host working directory.
given_when_then: Given uninitialized client or relative cwd, when creating session, then it is refused

behavior: Concurrent ACP requests are matched to their replies even when replies arrive out of order.
given_when_then: Given two in-flight requests, when replies arrive reversed, then each caller gets its own reply

behavior: A prompt streams text, diffs, terminal references and unknown update kinds without failing.
given_when_then: Given a prompt in flight, when updates arrive, then known ones are surfaced in order and unknown ones are tolerated

behavior: Permission selection only accepts an option the agent actually offered; cancel denies a pending permission and a late grant is ignored; a failing permission callback denies without exposing the error.
given_when_then: Given a permission request, when user picks an unoffered option, cancels, or the handler throws, then the result is deny/reject

behavior: Unsupported file-system, terminal and future agent requests are answered 'method not found'; terminal and future authentication cannot be invoked by this client.
given_when_then: Given agent asks for fs/terminal/unknown capability, when handled, then method-not-found is returned

behavior: End of stream, timeout, dispose or write failure completes or abandons every pending ACP request, and a timed-out prompt is never replayed.
given_when_then: Given pending calls, when connection ends or times out, then all complete with failure and nothing is re-sent

behavior: Oversized incoming input, oversized outgoing prompts, malformed frames and malformed matched results fail safely without stranding a waiter; a flood of unsupported requests closes the connection instead of growing memory.
given_when_then: Given bounds exceeded or garbage frames, when processed, then the call fails, nothing oversized is written, and the connection closes on flood

behavior: OpenCode 2 session and message lists walk pages by passing cursors back verbatim and parse the message union.
given_when_then: Given paged lists, when fetched, then all pages in order

behavior: Prompt send uses the v2 wire shape and returns the inbox receipt; session mutations use the v2 endpoints with 204 responses; location-scoped reads carry deep-object location params; permission and form replies post documented bodies; fs read returns raw bytes.
given_when_then: Given each call, when made, then method, path and body match v2 docs

behavior: Active sessions map to status types, malformed active snapshots are rejected, and tagged error envelopes surface as typed errors.
given_when_then: Given server replies, when mapped, then typed results or errors

behavior: The OpenCode 2 dialect layer passes unchanged requests untouched, adapts 2.1 moved routes, methods on parent resources, renamed fields, worktree project placement, and reshapes responses into what the beta call sites read; removed features fail clearly instead of 404.
given_when_then: Given a 2.1 server, when calling beta-shaped APIs, then requests are translated and removed ones error clearly

behavior: A captured OpenCode 2 prompt round-trip replays into typed events; unknown event types never throw; the log.synced boundary marker, permission, form, status, mcp and vcs events parse.
given_when_then: Given event fixtures, when parsed, then typed events or unknown fallback

behavior: Adapting v2 events to the common envelope maps the prompt round-trip, session idle, execution failure to session error (blank messages still get words), interrupted-run reasons, permission asked, tool input deltas, renames and refresh hints.
given_when_then: Given v2 events, when adapted, then app-level events match

behavior: OpenCode 2 capabilities are advertised per the port matrix.
given_when_then: Given v2 server, when capabilities read, then flags match matrix

behavior: Sessions, messages and parts map from captured v2 data: user text and attachments, assistant reasoning/text/tool content, tokens and cost, shell messages (status and shell id kept), failed shell as tool error, tool errors, output files, interleaved content order and streaming tool input.
given_when_then: Given captured fixtures, when mapped, then app message model matches

behavior: V2-only shapes (switch markers, synthetic/system/skill notices, compaction statuses, unknown variants) map to tagged notices without loss; 'default' variant reads as no variant; a live 2.1.1 page maps with native data.
given_when_then: Given v2-only message kinds, when mapped, then tagged parts or generic notice

behavior: Permissions, providers, models with modes, variants, agents, files, VCS diffs and status, errors and health map to the common model; reply strings map to the v2 wire enum.
given_when_then: Given v2 payloads, when mapped, then common model matches

behavior: The global session finder asks newest first and keeps the cursor after filtering.
given_when_then: Given filtered list, when paging, then cursor continues correctly

behavior: An unsupported health reply triggers connection re-detection.
given_when_then: Given odd health shape, when connecting, then redetect

behavior: Hidden OpenCode 2 form fields become preset answers and visible ones become prompts.
given_when_then: Given form fields, when shown, then hidden preset

behavior: Viewing a session posts the observed idle timestamp in the active location; ordinary prompt, command and shell keep server selection; explicit model selection replaces the model ref and creation uses defaults; a staged revert blocks prompts and commands before an implicit commit.
given_when_then: Given session actions, when sent, then wire carries expected fields

behavior: Forms and inbox: pending forms and inbox items list from the server, replies use session-scoped routes, steer/queue/cancel address item routes, 400 invalid answer and 409 already-settled/already-delivered surface as tagged errors, and events pass through.
given_when_then: Given forms/inbox, when acted on, then routes and typed errors match

behavior: Prompt delivery carries queue delivery when chosen and omits it for the default steer; permission replies forward or omit the reject message.
given_when_then: Given delivery or reject message, when sent, then wire includes or omits it

behavior: MCP scope: v2 rejects persistent scope and existing names without PUT; uniqueness read and add keep the same location across awaits.
given_when_then: Given MCP add, when scope persistent or duplicate, then refused

behavior: V2 models parse captured sessions, messages (union), prompt receipts, model/provider/agent/catalog listings, locations, fs listings, permissions, forms with six field types and conditions and error envelopes; unknown types and enum values never throw.
given_when_then: Given captured JSON, when parsed, then typed models without exceptions

behavior: Before sending, permission preparation succeeds or fails per send kind; automatic approval restores server rules before the message, switching it off mid-reply turns requests back on, a message right after server boot waits for the project; Auto-approve and Allow once send decision 'once'.
given_when_then: Given auto-approve toggles, when sending, then rules are in place first

behavior: Phone chat dispatch waits for admission before any request, settles an accepted dispatch exactly once, and settles uncertainty without replaying.
given_when_then: Given send, when accepted or uncertain, then settle once and never replay

behavior: Provider catalog handles a later failure while the first request waits; OAuth and MCP actions keep scope and confirm completed code sign-in.
given_when_then: Given concurrent catalog loads and OAuth, when one fails, then others still resolve

behavior: Reverting asks the server to restore files, stays undoable until committed, restoring clears the staged revert, stage returns a fixed preview and history-only preference, commit and clear use distinct endpoints.
given_when_then: Given revert, when staged/committed/cleared, then endpoints and state match

behavior: Session permission policy: fresh sessions use the server's default first; automatic sessions keep own rules including denials; key order is irrelevant; oversized policy is refused before writing; agent allowances and denials keep order; changing agent uses original rules; external edits replace saved original; malformed rules or provenance fail closed.
given_when_then: Given policy edits, when composed, then rules preserved or refused

behavior: SSE parsing handles bare data frames, keepalive comments, event field, multi-line data, CRLF and mid-line chunk boundaries, trailing frame only on flush, oversized frames dropped without harming the next, and a frame cut mid-write is discarded.
given_when_then: Given byte streams, when parsed, then complete frames only

behavior: The event stream delivers typed envelopes and reconnects; the session log stream tracks the durable sequence and surfaces log.synced.
given_when_then: Given drop, when reconnecting, then resume from seq and mark synced

behavior: Stable-line features are advertised: git init (409 counts as done), worktree create, and shell settings that list shells, patch only acceptable shells, refuse unlisted ones and clear with null.
given_when_then: Given 2.0.29 server, when used, then calls match

behavior: The terminal websocket uses the default Basic header and a single-use ticket; a bring-your-own-server proxy forwards the per-phone header; revocation after ticket issuance still rejects the socket.
given_when_then: Given terminal open, when ticket reused or revoked, then rejected

behavior: Server roots normalize trailing slashes and /api; Basic auth is built from the opencode user; credentials are never placed in a URL.
given_when_then: Given root and password, when requested, then header only

behavior: HTTP statuses map to typed errors: 401 auth required even with empty body, tagged envelopes with tag/status/extras, 503 boot as unavailable, refusal as network error.
given_when_then: Given error replies, when mapped, then typed

behavior: Connecting settles the server generation by its health answer without extra requests, and health sends Basic auth.
given_when_then: Given server, when connecting, then generation settled once

behavior: On OpenCode 2 a finished step is not a finished run; the run stays running until execution actually ends.
given_when_then: Given a step-finished event, then the run is still running

behavior: Prompt dispatch supplies the caller's command ID and, on OpenCode 1, confirms admission by finding the exact user message ID in history (including older pages); matching text with a wrong ID/session/role does not confirm; paging is bounded; capability off refuses without lookup; closed connection cannot confirm.
given_when_then: Given a sent prompt, then confirmed only by exact ID

behavior: On OpenCode 2 a prompt posts the client ID and validates its admission receipt; pending inbox or promoted message confirms; wrong session, type, message ID or mismatched receipt stays unconfirmed; session creation posts the supplied client ID.

behavior: A staged revert refuses prompting without committing the revert; a location change or policy fence between preflight and POST prevents the POST.
given_when_then: Given context changes after preflight, then nothing is sent

behavior: OpenCode 2 forms: a created event adds the form, replied/cancelled settle it, refresh hydrates pending ones, reply and cancel post and settle, an already-settled reply resolves locally, a 400 invalid answer keeps the form pending, and deleting a session drops its forms and inbox items.
given_when_then: Given form events, then pending list follows

behavior: OpenCode 2 inbox: enqueued/delivery.changed/delivered events project pending sends, refresh reconciles from REST, cancelling returns the text to the composer, a 409 already-delivered cancel drops the item, and changing the delivery mode updates the server and the UI.
given_when_then: Given inbox events, then pending sends match server

behavior: Notification Reply on an OpenCode 2 permission rejects with a message on the exact request; a stale request ID refreshes the alert instead of resolving; an empty reply is not delivered.
given_when_then: Given Reply from notification, then the matching request is rejected with text

behavior: Server installation events retain the exact available and installed versions.
given_when_then: Given an installation event, then both versions are kept

behavior: OpenCode 2 request replies (permission and question) wait for a woken transport, share one write slot, cannot cross a replacement connection, and a late failure after remote resolution shows no error; QuestionNotFound resolves locally; partial hydration failure keeps reply provenance; V2-only hydration blocks stale resurrection; a connected stream reconciles a missed idle event.
given_when_then: Given reconnect, then replies reach the right request

behavior: A connector search status 'catalogue off' is its own status.
given_when_then: Given catalogue disabled, then status is catalogue_off

behavior: List reads follow the next-page cursor until the end and pass the requested kind.
given_when_then: Given multi-page results, when listing, then all pages are fetched and kind is sent.

behavior: Thing ids are made path-safe before going into a request address.
given_when_then: Given an id with special characters, when requested, then it is encoded.

behavior: Search sends the words and tells the user locked notes were not searched.
given_when_then: Given a search, when answered, then the result flags locked notes as unsearched.

behavior: Node errors keep their code and request id (e.g. 501 not_enabled), a status with no body is named from the status, no answer is node_unreachable, and an unreadable answer is a plain failure rather than a crash.
given_when_then: Given each failure shape, when read, then a typed plain error is produced.

behavior: Every write carries an Idempotency-Key: capture and fact add/change use the caller's key with the contract bodies; retry, discard and outbox batch follow the contract; every other write gets a fresh key.
given_when_then: Given a write, when sent, then the key and body match the contract.

behavior: Reminder schedules go as structured JSON with the title in its own field and use the node's own repeat forms; a schedule read back keeps its form and unknown forms stay raw.
given_when_then: Given a schedule, when created/read, then the shape round-trips without loss.

behavior: Editing a reminder keeps its schedule id and may confirm a floating time zone; create sends the preview exactly as received with its digest; pause is a patch carrying the revision it was based on.
given_when_then: Given an edit/create/pause, when sent, then ids, digest and revision are included.

behavior: Pairing turns a code into a token with no Authorization header; a refused code is a plain failure; node info needs no credential.
given_when_then: Given a pairing code, when exchanged, then a token is stored or a plain failure shown.

behavior: Usage quota for the in-app Ubuntu server is read from loopback port 4195 with a Bearer token only; a remote server keeps its origin and Basic sign-in; with no token it reports unsupported and sends nothing; only the app's own server gets a token reader.
given_when_then: Given server kind / when quota is read / then right origin and auth, or nothing sent

behavior: OpenCode 2 shell reads use byte cursors, timeouts and delete while keeping workspace scope; discovery handles HTTP failures without advertising false support; shell lifecycle survives event projection without fake messages.
given_when_then: given shell API, when reading/deleting, then scoped and honest

behavior: A repository without message deletion stays a bounded error.
given_when_then: given no delete support, when deleting, then bounded error

behavior: OpenCode 2 message history opens newest first, one page at a time past the old cap, with cursor-only continuation.
given_when_then: given long history, when opened, then newest page then cursor

behavior: Model refs normalise: bare IDs strip only their own provider prefix, composite OpenCode 2 IDs are sent bare, already-bare refs are unchanged.
given_when_then: given composite model id, when sent, then bare

behavior: The OpenCode 2 migration status maps its four answers, accepts the server's data envelope and rejects unknown shapes; the page shows plain words and keeps server text out; the gateway reads it from the migration endpoint.
given_when_then: Given a migration status response, when read, then one of four states shows in plain words and unknown shapes are rejected

behavior: A pairing payload from the server parses into addresses, password and username; addresses keep server order, are trimmed and de-duplicated; clipboard whitespace is tolerated; a missing or blank username means the default user; a custom username is kept.
given_when_then: Given a real pairing payload, when parsed, then addresses, password and username are correct

behavior: Every malformed pairing payload yields an honest failure and never a crash: empty, bad JSON, non-object, wrong types, empty or blank address lists, too many addresses, bad password or username, huge input, huge address, deep nesting; no failure message echoes the input.

given_when_then: Given multiple candidate addresses, when pairing, then the first valid working host is chosen and each failure has its own reason

behavior: A scanned QR carrying a pairing code is handled exactly like a pasted code; a QR that is not a pairing code is rejected with a reason.
given_when_then: Given a scanned QR, when read, then it follows the paste path or is rejected plainly

behavior: Probing a Paseo host: bad input never opens a socket and a verified daemon names its ready runtimes.
given_when_then: Given an address, when probed, then invalid input is rejected without network and valid hosts list runtimes

behavior: Hello rejection: wrong or missing password reads as authentication failure, incompatible protocol is named plainly, unknown reasons are a plain disconnect, close code alone still maps; the handshake advertises rejection support and the password only when set; unknown frames are ignored; old and new daemons and the previous and current Claude Code pins are accepted.
given_when_then: Given a rejection or version, when handshaking, then the right plain error or acceptance results

behavior: The native transport reuses its socket after a short pause; large JSON decoding preserves data with and without a length header.
given_when_then: Given keep-alive pause, when next request, then same socket; large JSON intact

behavior: Permission requests parse the current contract and legacy permission events keep their identity; tool states expose pending input and error text; concurrent requests and session statuses are tracked.
given_when_then: Given current and legacy events, when parsed, then same request identity

behavior: Answering an externally resolved permission is idempotent.

behavior: A safe snapshot of the report is a point-in-time record that does not change after it is taken.
given_when_then: Given a snapshot, when underlying records change, then the snapshot stays the same.

behavior: A crash report holds at most 20 records and stays within a fixed UTF-8 byte budget.
given_when_then: Given more than 20 records or oversized text, when building, then it is trimmed to 20 records and the byte cap.

behavior: Sharing a report opens the share sheet with exactly the previewed text and writes nothing locally.
given_when_then: Given an issued preview, when the user shares, then the exact previewed text is handed to the share sheet.

behavior: A preview can only be authorized by the preview issued for the current evidence: new objects, another builder, changed evidence, a controller replacement or a storage failure all make an old preview stale and require a fresh preview before sharing.
given_when_then: Given an issued preview, when evidence changes or the controller is replaced, then sharing is refused until previewed again.

behavior: If capture is cleared while the report is loading, the report is not shared.
given_when_then: Given a share in flight, when capture is cleared, then nothing is shared.

behavior: When the report cannot be loaded, sharing is rejected or throws, or the platform has no share channel, the user gets a fixed plain outcome (unavailable / share unavailable) and no report text or private error.
given_when_then: Given a loader, share or platform failure, when sharing, then a fixed outcome appears without details.

behavior: Two overlapping share requests open the share sheet only once; the second returns busy.
given_when_then: Given a share in progress, when a second share is requested, then it reports busy.

behavior: A credential loaded from storage is masked in persisted diagnostics and in reports.
given_when_then: Given a stored credential, when diagnostics or a report are written, then the secret is masked.

behavior: A new or updated credential is registered for redaction before it is stored or used, even if secure storage then fails, including passwords of new authenticated transports and submitted provider keys.
given_when_then: Given a new secret, when storage fails or a request starts, then the secret is already redacted from output.

behavior: Default notices have one owner per preference store and profile, and writes for an absent profile are rejected.
given_when_then: Given a profile, when notice state is written, then one owner handles it; with no profile the write is rejected.

behavior: The in-app preview may load only the same host and port, never a non-http(s) scheme, and never a URL with embedded credentials.
given_when_then: Given a navigation request, when checked, then only the same http(s) host:port without credentials is allowed.

behavior: Device diagnostics separates helper-process deaths from Android app exits; history is repeatable and never consumes launch-recovery data.
given_when_then: Given exit records, when shown, then helper deaths and app exits are distinct and history is re-readable.

behavior: The diagnostics report preview stays off until consent and shares exact safe text; clearing captured evidence invalidates a preview; listeners are told when the background owner pauses.
given_when_then: Given consent state changes, when previewing or sharing, then it reflects only current consented evidence.

behavior: Project-file references require a matching location and are never read locally; invalid identities and temporary references cannot escape the attachment store.
given_when_then: Given a path-like or foreign reference, when resolved, then it is refused and no file outside the store is touched.

behavior: External agent requests never forward credentials on redirect or to another origin, omit the bearer for public or unauthenticated calls, and reject unsafe addresses before any network call.
given_when_then: Given a redirect or unsafe address, when requested, then no credential leaks and no request is made.

behavior: Deleting an external agent removes its credential and records, and late responses or in-flight requests cannot recreate them; a failed credential deletion leaves an unavailable marker and retries cleanly; no bearer token appears in persisted registry or task snapshots.
given_when_then: Given agent deletion, when late data arrives or deletion fails, then no secret or record resurrects.

behavior: Only https (and http with a warning) links open; every other scheme, embedded credentials, hostless, empty, unparseable or overlong URLs are refused before reaching the platform.
given_when_then: Given a URL from a server or form, when opened, then unsafe values are refused.

behavior: The link confirmation names the host and shows the port only when the URL includes one; sign-in pages and external links open through the one safe opener.
given_when_then: Given a link, when confirming, then host(:port) is shown and opening goes through the safe path.

behavior: Ed25519 signing matches the RFC 8032 test vectors, and a seed of the wrong length is refused.
given_when_then: Given RFC vectors, when signing, then signatures match exactly.

behavior: JSON canonicalization follows RFC 8785: keys sorted by code unit, no whitespace, integers kept, only required escapes, non-integer numbers refused, UTF-8 bytes.
given_when_then: Given JSON, when canonicalized, then bytes match the standard.

behavior: The owner signer produces a proof with signer, nonce, time and a 128-hex signature that covers only the canonical envelope; the nonce is fresh every time.
given_when_then: Given an envelope, when signed twice, then proofs differ in nonce and verify over the canonical bytes.

behavior: Memory-node addresses must be private (default port applied); public, odd or credential-bearing addresses are refused.
given_when_then: Given an address, when entered, then private ones parse and others are refused.

behavior: The fixed signature vector holds: our canonical envelope bytes equal the vector, the signature verifies with its public key, every listed refusal is a change that breaks the signature, and the root key hashes to its fingerprint.
given_when_then: Given the vector, when verified and tampered, then it verifies only unmodified.

behavior: The control chain is trusted only against the pinned fingerprint: the node's chain verifies fingerprint, pin, signatures and links; a replacement fingerprint offered by the node is not accepted; a changed record, order or fork is not trusted.
given_when_then: Given a chain, when tampered or re-pinned, then trust is refused.

behavior: A share the owner did not sign is kept encrypted and no rule fires from it.
given_when_then: Given an unsigned share, when stored, then it is encrypted and triggers no rule.

behavior: Before an owner signature the person authenticates; the signed authentication time is when they authenticated, the prompt uses the app's words, and a refused prompt means nothing is signed or sent.
given_when_then: Given a signing action, when the device prompt is refused, then nothing is signed or sent.

behavior: Device authentication results map to plain outcomes: success with time, no screen lock/biometric set up or no plugin is 'unavailable', backing out/timeout/interruption is 'cancelled', too many tries is 'locked', anything else 'failed'.
given_when_then: Given platform auth results, when mapped, then outcomes are one of the five.

behavior: The memory vault passphrase is generated once, kept in secure storage not on disk, reused, migrated from an old file (which is then deleted), handed to the node at start without leaving a file, and deleted when the memory is removed.
given_when_then: Given a vault, when created, upgraded or removed, then the passphrase lives only in secure storage.

behavior: Disconnecting forgets the token, key and record but keeps the outbox; the owner key is made once, kept in secure storage and only its public half shown.
given_when_then: Given disconnect, when done, then secrets are erased, outbox kept; the public key is the only one shown.

behavior: The FactsBook node bearer token is sent only in a request header, never in the URL.
given_when_then: Given a token, when any read is made, then the Authorization header carries it and the address has none.

behavior: Owner review decisions are signed and bound to the digest and preconditions; an edited proposal sends the edit; without an owner key the call never leaves the phone; area sharing reads the policy revision and signs the area; a stale approval is named as stale.
given_when_then: Given a review decision, when sent, then it is signed or refused locally and stale approvals are named.

behavior: Log excerpts are redacted over the whole multiline input before truncation and keep a bounded tail, including when one line is huge.
given_when_then: Given secrets in a long log, when excerpted, then secrets are masked and size bounded.

behavior: Never auto-allow when the gateway or daemon is unqualified, the raw name/tool kind is not exact, or the session is foreign, unknown or non-Claude.
given_when_then: Given an unqualified or foreign request, then the ordinary permission prompt remains.

behavior: The GitHub token reaches git only through a private (0600) file in a private (0700) randomly named folder, one per command, never in a script or URL and never used without that file; it is removed after success, failure or a bridge error; no push happens if the file cannot be made private or no Linux is installed; the credential helper names only the variable.
given_when_then: Given any push outcome, then the token exists only in a private one-command file and nothing is left behind.

behavior: On built-in Linux, push hands the signed-in GitHub token to the drop and a rejected token signs the account out; on Termux and servers no sign-in is offered and the token stays home; abilities follow the snapshot.
given_when_then: Given the workspace kind, then token use matches.

behavior: Shell quoting stops every expansion, refuses NUL bytes without echoing the value, quotes every word, renders the exact script, validates step and variable names, decodes step envelopes ignoring noise, reports cut-off answers, and checks folder and git availability.
given_when_then: Given hostile input, then it stays literal.

behavior: GitHub sign-in walks its states and stores the token under the profile key; a failed attempt says why and stores nothing; cancel ignores a late token; sign-out or a rejected token forgets it; an expired token is refreshed and the new pair stored.
given_when_then: Given device sign-in, then token stored/forgotten as described.

behavior: Removing a profile deletes its GitHub sign-in, and 'reset saved sign-ins' deletes every GitHub sign-in.
given_when_then: Given profile deletion, then GitHub token is gone.

behavior: GitHub sign-in by device code requests a code with the app's public client id and no secret, polls at the server interval, and returns the token plus login; the code and token never appear in printed text.
given_when_then: Given GitHub answers pending, pending, slow_down, token / when polling / then waits 5s,5s,10s,10s and ends signed in as the login

behavior: A slow-down answer with no interval adds five seconds to the wait.
given_when_then: Given interval 2 and slow_down / when polling / then waits 2s then 7s

behavior: Device sign-in ends with a typed reason for each failure: code expired (by server or by local clock), access denied, device flow switched off for the app, rejected token on the user lookup.
given_when_then: Given each GitHub error / when polling / then the matching typed problem is raised

behavior: A brief network failure while polling is retried; three in a row end the sign-in; cancelling stops before the next poll.
given_when_then: Given network errors / when polling / then retry up to three consecutive failures; cancel stops

behavior: Expiring GitHub tokens are refreshed by rotating the pair while keeping the login.
given_when_then: Given an expiring token / when refreshed / then new access and refresh tokens are stored and the login is kept

behavior: Repair only reaches the projects folder, never a Termux path outside a proot-distro store, and the Termux script uploads nothing outside a store. Pack files are verified by trailing checksum.
given_when_then: Given a path outside the store / when repair runs / then it is refused; pack with bad checksum is rejected

behavior: Pinned scripts and guides use a full commit hash with a checked checksum, check the download before naming/running it, install the official pinned OpenCode 2 package, and nothing shown pipes a download into a shell.
given_when_then: Given each pinned script / when inspected / then hash is full, checksum matches, no curl|sh

behavior: Deleting a profile removes its consent record and leaves other servers intact; corrupt or unwritable storage never offers consent or records a grant.
given_when_then: Given profile delete or bad storage / when read / then removed or safe-denied

behavior: Redaction masks registered secrets (6+ chars) anywhere, longest first, literally, idempotently, cleared on demand; masks provider keys (sk-, ghp_, xox, AIza, JWT), Authorization/Bearer/Basic/Digest values, key=value passwords incl. quoted, URL credentials; keeps JSON valid; leaves paths, SHAs, UUIDs and ordinary words alone.
given_when_then: Given text with secrets / when displayed or copied / then replaced by mask

behavior: Provider key-page links are official https pages; the OAuth authorization URL policy accepts only HTTPS hosts without embedded credentials; provider OAuth completion accepts either a bare code or a pasted callback URL.
given_when_then: Given a provider link or OAuth input / when validating / then only credential-free https passes and code or callback URL completes

behavior: Scripts that run in Linux refuse unsafe input: tail refuses anything that is not a plain file path, a quote in a path cannot end the quoting, package scripts refuse text that is not a package name, and cleanup names only safe paths.
given_when_then: Given hostile text in a path or package name / when building a shell script / then it is refused or safely quoted

behavior: The on-phone agent daemon runs as an ordinary user, listens on loopback only with relay off, never widens, never downloads speech models, and receives its password never as an argument and never traced.
given_when_then: given the daemon launch, when inspected, then non-root, loopback, no password in args or trace

behavior: Native sign-in errors never expose platform or CLI text.
given_when_then: given native failure, when shown, then fixed words

behavior: A plain project export leaves out every credential; a private export adds credentials and OpenCode data but not logs; the file name says when private; credential names are recognised wherever they are.
given_when_then: given export, when plain, then no credentials

behavior: Connector gateway errors never expose raw credential text; dispose never revokes server credentials; explicit invalidation cannot be undone by returning to the source.
given_when_then: given gateway error, when shown, then no credential text

behavior: Connector OAuth is explicit, uses validated codes and state, fails closed when OAuth is off or launch unsafe, cancels only owned authentication, never exposes late launch or the code, needs setup when client registration fails, and asks for a manual return URL when the callback port is busy.
given_when_then: given OAuth flow, when callback arrives, then validated; unsafe fails closed

behavior: Header values in connector setup are secrets and diagnostics redact Authorization=Bearer values.
given_when_then: given header secret, when diagnostics, then redacted

behavior: An error headline drops the class name and stack trace.
given_when_then: given exception, when headlined, then plain text

behavior: Raw exception or protocol text is never shown as copy: the domain mapper never promotes protocol text, the product error mapper depends only on domain categories, and the allowlist only shrinks.
given_when_then: given any error, when shown, then plain authored words

behavior: Permission notifications show on the shade only, name the program and sub-command or the file with the right verb, never put a secret from the command in the title or body, have no target when there is nothing to show, and use the subtitle server · project with either optional.
given_when_then: Given a permission ask, when notified, then the target is named, secrets are masked and the subtitle follows the rule.

behavior: Notification text keeps ordinary commands whole but masks bearer tokens, provider keys, passwords, URL credentials (keeping host) and long token-like runs, keeps the key name, and is one ellipsised line.
given_when_then: given secret text, when notified, then masked

behavior: The pairing credential is held carefully: printing redacts the password and strips credentials and query secrets from addresses, does not echo untrusted usernames, can be consumed to drop the reference, and the address list cannot be mutated.
given_when_then: Given a parsed pairing payload, when logged or consumed, then no secret appears and the password is dropped

behavior: When no address answers, the failure gives a reason per address, with URL secrets and arbitrary probe text stripped and safe IPv6 origins kept readable.
given_when_then: Given all addresses failing, when reported, then each has a safe plain reason

behavior: ACP permission choices expose only offered one-call actions: allow-once echoes the offered ID and stores no standing approval, default denial uses reject-once or interrupts instead of falling to always, standing or unoffered IDs and unknown option kinds never grant, contradictory actions or a spoofed native provider cannot bypass the mapping, and disconnected permissions cannot be answered via a new connection.
given_when_then: Given an ACP permission request, when answering, then only exact offered one-time options are sent and ambiguity denies

behavior: Raw agent errors and diagnostic text never reach events or history; encrypted public endpoints are rejected while private endpoints stay usable.
given_when_then: Given an agent error or public endpoint, when handled, then only safe fixed copy is shown and public endpoints are refused

behavior: Handoff writes its transfer record only into a new exclusively created folder, verifies the ignore entry before writing conversation content, never overwrites or reuses an existing folder or ignore file, refuses parent symlinks, requires the negotiated feature and a live connection, and rejects invalid scope, paths and byte limits.
given_when_then: Given an unsafe or invalid transfer target, when handing off, then nothing is written or dispatched

behavior: Browser authority is revoked on abort, delete, new-chat replacement, close, profile revoke and session deletion; reopening retires the old generation keeping the agent id; cleanup quarantine preserves intent without an ordinary fallback; cancel or delete during cold creation never resurrects a turn; trusted folder rebinding keeps old intent.
given_when_then: Given browser authority, when the chat ends or changes, then authority is revoked and no stale send occurs

behavior: Paseo endpoints: cleartext is limited to this device and Tailscale; profile validators agree and an empty password is allowed; a profile round-trips without storing its password in plain profile data; a rejected password is an authentication failure.
given_when_then: Given an endpoint and password, when validated or stored, then cleartext is limited and passwords are kept apart

behavior: Paseo permissions: a write request becomes an edit card with its file; once allows while always also applies the provider rule; reject denies with the reason and cancel also interrupts; a typed rejection reads as declined; an answered request does not return from a stale snapshot and one answered elsewhere is retired; permission mapping covers shell and unknown tools.
given_when_then: Given a permission request, when answered, then exactly the chosen decision is sent and stale prompts vanish

behavior: Native Paseo permissions: a same-id command or rule replaces the pending permission, snapshots detach data, hidden rule or input changes invalidate a captured approval, malformed replacements retire the actionable permission, resolve and disconnect retire revisions without resending, location change and deletion retire permissions, and feed attention updates without refresh.
given_when_then: Given a changing permission, when approving, then only the exact current revision can be approved

behavior: Turning usage off, runtime gating and profile deletion clear or stop the monitor and delete the opt-in and widget snapshot.
given_when_then: Given enabled monitor, when disabled or profile deleted, then snapshot removed

behavior: Performance diagnostics redact secret-named attributes and token-like values, drop ids and query values from paths, and label the password script generically.
given_when_then: Given secrets in spans, when exported, then redacted

behavior: The engine client refuses remote hosts, userinfo and credential newlines before any network call; authenticates every endpoint with redirects disabled and never exposes redirect bodies; wrong-profile or unknown-schema health is rejected without raw details; commands are redacted before transmission and ambiguous mutations never retried.
given_when_then: Given unsafe host or redirect, when called, then refused with no leak

behavior: Private IPv4 ranges (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, link-local etc.) are private and their neighbours are not; IPv6 unique-local and link-local are private; only .local names count as private names.
given_when_then: Given addresses and names, when classified, then private or not exactly per ranges.

behavior: Plain http to a private address is accepted (with credentials); public addresses and other names need explicit HTTP consent; loopback and https never need confirmation; a bare private address still gains https.
given_when_then: Given a server URL, when validated, then consent requirement follows the rule.

behavior: The HTTP confirmation is recorded against one exact origin; moving the profile to another address drops it; a different private origin is not covered; confirming survives a rebuilt profile and a reload.
given_when_then: Given a confirmed origin, when address changes or reloads, then confirmation applies only to the exact origin.

behavior: Connection advice distinguishes private, Tailscale and public HTTP.
given_when_then: Given three address kinds, when advice is shown, then different text per kind.

behavior: Codex and Paseo stay HTTPS-only off this device: a private address is refused over ws://.
given_when_then: Given a private ws address for Codex/Paseo, when added, then refused.

behavior: Pairing with a private http address is held, never probed, until confirmed; public HTTP pairing waits for explicit origin consent.
given_when_then: Given pairing to http, when unconfirmed, then no network probe.

behavior: An unconfirmed private http profile is blocked, connect refuses it in plain words, and the deletion sweep removes the confirmation key.
given_when_then: Given an unconfirmed profile, when connecting, then a plain refusal; when deleted, key removed.

behavior: A problem report carries title, description, the attached error and environment; the first description line becomes the title when no error; a bounded number of errors, timings and stack lines are kept; platform label and version fallback exist.
given_when_then: Given an error, when a report is built, then these fields are present and bounded.

behavior: The report's connection detail is scrubbed and a failed job report carries no timing traces; the persisted store and in-memory list feed the same events.
given_when_then: Given a connection and a failed job, when reported, then scrubbed with no traces.

behavior: A report never contains a credential or a server address (fake provider keys, bearer tokens, passwords, registered values are masked).
given_when_then: Given secrets in an error, when reported, then none appears.

behavior: A short report is prefilled whole in the GitHub link through the safe external-link policy; long diagnostics go to the clipboard with the form saying to paste; a very long description copies the whole report.
given_when_then: Given report size, when sent, then prefilled link, or clipboard with instruction.

behavior: Errors are shown in plain words: product messages pass through, a 502 and other statuses are said in words with raw text only in Details, API exception messages and server prose never become body text, and OpenCode 2 failures too.
given_when_then: Given an error, when shown, then plain words and details separate.

behavior: The app's own staged-revert sentence is kept, but a staged-revert tag never permits arbitrary protocol prose.
given_when_then: Given the tag with foreign prose, when shown, then only the app's sentence.

behavior: Plain strings are words; raw failure strings are classified; invalid-state errors are said plainly without blaming the network; socket errors collapse to one connectivity line; timeouts, storage failures and a missing keyring have their own words; device failures hide native text; native/Termux output becomes words while app sentences stay.
given_when_then: Given each failure kind, when shown, then the specific plain line.

behavior: Error details are redacted, and a transport failure offers the network fix; shared error parts show words, not the raw failure.
given_when_then: Given a failure, when displayed, then redacted Details and a fix action.

behavior: A Linux keyring failure surfaces as secure-storage-unavailable while other platforms give the generic device sentence; the keyring probe only reports a Linux desktop without one.
given_when_then: Given a keyring failure, when shown, then platform-specific wording.

behavior: The Codex token is stored apart from the password and JSON; a missing token requests re-entry without exposing metadata; a failed token save or delete rolls the metadata back; deletion removes only its token.
given_when_then: Given Codex profile ops, when storage fails, then metadata is rolled back.

behavior: Codex origins and bounds (directory, token) are validated without echoing input; profile deletion sweeps BYO vault and metadata only for that profile; a private transport lease cannot persist its address or credential.
given_when_then: Given invalid or leased values, when saved, then rejected or not persisted, with no echo.

behavior: Logo downloads reject oversize, wrong type, non-200 and active content; the default sparkle means no logo and is remembered.
given_when_then: Given bad responses, when fetched, then no logo.

behavior: The quota client rejects unsafe origins and raw empty userinfo, has no empty-password or ambiguous Basic fallback, allows approved loopback forms with auth, and preserves an empty user.
given_when_then: Given odd origins or credentials, when called, then rejected or sent exactly.

behavior: HTTP failures are status-only, never follow redirects or probe fallbacks; JSON, UTF-8, schema and account mismatches become safe failures; transport and stream errors never expose raw errors, URLs or credentials.
given_when_then: Given failures, when handled, then safe sanitized failure.

behavior: Response size is capped at exactly 64 KiB, oversize chunks are refused, and streaming stops an oversized source early before buffering; close is idempotent, settles waiting reads and cancels a partial body.
given_when_then: Given big bodies or close, when reading, then bounded and clean.

behavior: The collector token is long, random, stored securely and staged 0600; no command or service script holds the token or a key; OpenCode 2 looks in its own data folder first; the secure slot and switch are swept with the profile.
given_when_then: Given setup, when inspecting commands and files, then no secrets and tight permissions.

behavior: Read-state sharing consent: a missing legacy default migrates only the initial saved population, a malformed legacy value cannot grant sharing, explicit destination choices are preserved, refused migration completion stays private and retries, an interrupted cohort does not absorb later profiles, and consent is never optimistically true before disk acknowledgment.
given_when_then: Given legacy settings, when migrated, then sharing stays off unless acknowledged.

behavior: A failed opt-out stays private and persists on explicit retry; deletion drains a pending grant, prunes its journal and sweeps both keys; failed journal pruning is retryable and never restores consent.
given_when_then: Given opt-out or delete, when storage fails, then privacy preserved.

behavior: The redactor masks every fake credential in the fixtures (the gate is not vacuous).
given_when_then: Given fake keys, when redacted, then all masked.

behavior: Every verbatim (non-redacted) copy in the app is reviewed, the reviewed lists only shrink, each entry has a real reason, and the scan detects it in code but not in comments.
given_when_then: Given source, when scanned, then unreviewed verbatim copies fail.

behavior: Release URL policy requires explicit consent for remote HTTP, IPv6 loopback is loopback everywhere, and bare IPv6 addresses normalize into usable URLs.
given_when_then: Given URLs, when normalized, then policy applies.

behavior: Repeated permission consent: the third distinct ask offers 'always allow' once, survives restart and explains a decline; capability and exact scope gate offers across sessions without storing secrets; corrupt storage and refused writes suppress offers.
given_when_then: Given repeated asks, when counted, then offer rules hold.

behavior: Diagnostics report captures buffered errors and timings from before startup exactly once, keeps repeated errors, and keeps long-running spans that finish after newer ones
given_when_then: Given buffered events, when the report starts, then each is imported once

behavior: Provider keys and any registered secrets are redacted from trace output, thermal readings, stream errors, platform callbacks, device logs, notifications and log copy, at write time and again on recovery, before any length truncation
given_when_then: Given a secret, when it appears in any diagnostic source, then no output contains it

behavior: No keystores, signing secrets or third-party skill packs are committed
given_when_then: Given the tree, when scanned, then none are found

behavior: Saving a prompt redacts copy, encoded text payload and filename metadata before persistence
given_when_then: Given a fake credential in a prompt, when saved, then not stored

behavior: Cold-connection scheduled runs record a refused certificate as its own code, keep the approved certificate, reach an allowed plain-HTTP server, refuse one nobody allowed, refuse missing Codex credential before opening a socket; renaming a profile keeps trust fingerprint but endpoint edits invalidate it
given_when_then: Given trust choices, when run, then honored exactly

behavior: Trust origin includes effective port and ignores path; URLs with credentials, query or fragment are rejected; loopback needs no consent while every remote HTTP origin needs its own explicit choice; a certificate pin cannot be downgraded to HTTP; SHA-256 pins must be complete and accept colon formatting
given_when_then: Given URLs, when trust evaluated, then correct requirement

behavior: Public-HTTP choice and certificate pin survive restart and rebuild; another profile never inherits a pin; changing host, port or scheme removes the pin; malformed or wrong-origin persisted pins never restore trust
given_when_then: Given a pinned server, when host changes, then pin removed

behavior: Session-address links (shared with the server's address): unavailable in production capability; receive, duplicate and cancel are silent; binding requires approval before any authenticated lookup; unverified deployment makes zero discovery or credential calls; bearer-ID and unverified gateways are never queried
given_when_then: Given a link, when opened without approval, then nothing contacted

behavior: Sender emits only three fields (no profile or credentials) and only with disclosure and a current binding
given_when_then: Given share, when built, then only three fields

behavior: Address-link format: strict envelope, keys, percent escapes, single decode, bounded ASCII; only structurally valid full private HTTPS origins accepted; credential-bearing input rejected not repaired; a secret registered later still cannot be serialized
given_when_then: Given a link string, when parsed, then strict result

behavior: Address discovery uses anonymous exact requests pinned to a checked IP, accepts only tailnet addresses (v4 100.64/10 and v6), refuses public or mixed DNS and changed DNS, never follows redirects, types certificate failures without raw host, bounds responses, fails closed on malformed descriptors, and a late DNS cannot start a socket; every deployment proof is required
given_when_then: Given non-tailnet address, when discovered, then refused before connecting

behavior: Directories with spaces, shell metacharacters or single quotes are shell-quoted safely in the resume command; control characters in a directory are refused.
given_when_then: Given a directory with quotes or control characters, when building the command, then it is safely quoted or refused.

behavior: Session ids that could read as flags or shell text are refused for the resume command.
given_when_then: Given an id like '--foo' or with shell text, when building, then refused.

behavior: Blank, control-character or malformed references and destinations, duplicate messages and malformed identifying data are rejected; redaction and parent are identified without discarding the source.
given_when_then: Given bad import data, when reviewing, then it is rejected with no data loss on good parts.

behavior: Credentials and recognized secrets never enter session-link binding storage.
given_when_then: Given a binding with a secret, when saved, then the secret is absent.

behavior: Private read state stays local and ignores other clients' receipts; failed server sync keeps local read state and retries only on explicit observation; a newly opened viewer can finish after a covered viewer cancels.
given_when_then: Given private mode or sync failure, when viewing, then local state holds.

behavior: New profiles start private and consent changes only the named profile; revoking sharing elsewhere stops a waiting receipt; a transmitted receipt cannot acknowledge after revocation; delayed opt-in then opt-out never leaves sharing on; failed opt-out stays private.
given_when_then: Given consent toggles, when racing, then private always wins.

behavior: Reads strip credentials in environment variables and raw server errors; secret inputs and overlapping patches fail validation; malformed scalar and MCP inputs are rejected.
given_when_then: Given a config with secrets, when read or edited, then redacted or rejected.

behavior: Setup diagnostics and failure Details redact credentials; package repair failures keep their reason in Details without raw output.
given_when_then: Given a failure with credentials, when shown, then redacted.

behavior: Credential-shaped URLs, cleartext external URLs, secret or unknown inputs and split secret CLI arguments are never proposed or retained; unsupported workflows state the gap; closed or evicted sessions cannot resume.
given_when_then: Given a risky input, when planning, then refused.

behavior: By default, refresh and offline mode never touch the internet; an explicit refresh uses a fixed unauthenticated origin; opting out or going offline never fetches; a search term that looks like a credential is not sent.
given_when_then: Given default settings, when loading the registry, then no network call.

behavior: Registry metadata redaction drops credentials, unsafe URLs and executable arguments; declared header and variable names are kept but never values; package-only listings explain the unsupported install path.
