given_when_then: Given OpenCode 2.2.2, when the picker is built, then the trial is not offered.

behavior: The Claude Agent link script refuses an invalid agent home id, points at the shared agent home without touching the sign-in or printing secrets, and only its result line counts as success.
given_when_then: Given an agent home id ../x, when the script is built, then it is refused.

behavior: Claude Code on the phone is installed at its tested pinned version, never the latest from npm, and a different version ending up installed is a failure that names both versions.
given_when_then: Given a pin, when Claude Code installs and another version lands, then install fails naming pinned and installed versions

behavior: AI Team task conversations speak in role voices: each engine status line maps to manager, developer or reviewer; the planner is the architect while planning and when its plan is ready; unknown lines stay the manager's with the engine's words; the current line is the task's newest one unless the task status says otherwise; the developer is named by the task's role.
given_when_then: Given team timeline lines, when shown, then each is voiced by its role

behavior: The OpenCode 2 live proof talks only to the loopback server it was given: the password travels only in the Basic Authorization header, never in the address or query; outside or credential-bearing addresses are refused before any request; redirects are never followed with credentials; a failed HTTP body never enters an error or a result (only a code such as http_401); stable 2.x is detected only from a shaped /api/info after a healthy /api/health, and an unauthorized health is not followed; the stable permission reply is POST /api/session/<id>/permission/<id>/reply with a decision body; an event-stream reconnect sends no Last-Event-ID or after cursor; a generated server password is read only from an exact complete 'server password' line of 43 base64url characters.
given_when_then: Given a server that answers 401 with a secret in the body, when the live proof reads it, then the result holds only http_401 and no secret

behavior: Live proof model choice is honest: the model catalog is read again until an initial empty plugin snapshot settles and a requested model is enabled; an empty catalog after the bounded wait fails as 'enabled model missing' and a missing requested model fails as 'configured model unavailable' even when others exist; an explicit enabled model chosen by the person overrides the backend default and is the model the reply carries; a backend default that keeps retrying (HTTP 503) times out unqualified and is never silently replaced; model switch and image checks record the retrying alternative but stay failed with no fallback; a model kept without an owned model-selected event fails at selection; a switch prefers the selected provider and an image check the selected model, then the selected provider before others.
given_when_then: Given a backend default that retries 503 ten times, when the stream check runs, then it times out unqualified and no other model is used

behavior: A live proof passes a reply only on real completed inference: a fresh assistant message on the owned session, completed with a real completion time, finish normalised to 'stop' (a raw finish cannot override it), no error, from exactly the wanted model and variant, plus a fresh text delta from that session; prompt admission, catalog admission, an execution-success event, a foreign or stale delta, a user echo, synthetic text, or another model's answer never qualifies; OpenCode 2 replies are read in their flat type/content shape, not the legacy role/parts shape; diagnostics export only true/false facts and counts.
given_when_then: Given an execution-success event but no completed assistant message, when the stream check runs, then it fails as completed assistant missing

behavior: Live proof sessions are owned: each created session keeps the phase title with a unique ordinal and is written to the ownership ledger as it is created; if the ledger write fails, the created ID is kept and the check fails before any prompt is sent.
given_when_then: Given the ledger write fails after a session is created, when the check runs, then no prompt is sent and the ID is retained

behavior: A live abort check passes only when a running owned session with a fresh owned delta is interrupted and the session takes a usable next turn; an interrupt answered false on an idle session is never a pass, and execution start without an owned delta never sends an interrupt.
given_when_then: Given an idle session, when abort is checked, then it fails as abort requires running session

behavior: After a live reconnect the proof refetches owned state (sessions, messages, permissions and forms) and the event stream carries only the location directory, never replay parameters.
given_when_then: Given a reconnect, when the stream reopens, then its query holds only the location and owned state is refetched

behavior: Live permission checks use real requests from owned disposable sessions: on stable servers those sessions alone carry a shell ask rule (no config change, and beta servers get no stable-only rule); Allow replies 'once' and proves the shell call completed with exit 0, untruncated, with exactly the expected output and the 'Command exited with code 0.' line; Reject replies 'reject' and proves the call ended in error, no execution success, and the run ended interrupted; afterwards nothing is pending or active; a foreign session, request, call or reply, a wrong command, a missing reply or a retained call still pending or running fails, and so does any success, progress or command start after a reject; a foreign permission is never answered.
given_when_then: Given a permission asked by another session, when Allow is checked, then no reply is sent and the check fails

behavior: A live image check passes only when the user message kept exactly one PNG with the exact sent bytes (not a JPEG, a data address, a second file or bad base64) and the answer names the panel colours exactly, as one JSON object or one whole JSON fence; extra keys, wrong case, swapped colours, prose around it or a plain 'Image received' fail.
given_when_then: Given an answer 'Image received.', when the image check runs, then it fails as image content answer missing

behavior: A live card check passes only with a fresh, completed card tool call on the owned session, location, message and call (a local MCP call marked not executed counts when completed), from the wanted model, plus a retained user receipt carrying the actual tool call ID, and an acknowledgement; the MCP card helper must be connected and belong to the requested location or the check fails before any prompt; pending, running, errored, malformed or fabricated calls fail.
given_when_then: Given the card helper needs sign-in, when the card check runs, then it fails before any prompt

behavior: Live proof observation counts only fresh events of the owned session in the owned location (a global event without a location counts only for the owned session); failures become fixed counters (no route, model unavailable, provider auth), card diagnostics tell a nested ask from a helper rejection, a 503 retry counts only from a structured status or an exact status line, each counter saturates at 10000 on its own, and each snapshot counts only from its own start.
given_when_then: Given a retry from another session, when observed, then it is not counted

behavior: Live proof cleanup touches only what it created: a durable ownership ledger is written before sessions are created and records each ID; cleanup deletes only recorded IDs or sessions with the exact phase title and directory, treats 404 as gone, keeps the ID when the session's scope disagrees, never touches a person's sessions, and for a retired protocol keeps the ledger without sending anything; the ledger refuses links, conflicting intents, malformed or oversized evidence, stays readable across builds, and is removed only when empty.
given_when_then: Given a person's conversation on the server, when cleanup runs, then it is not deleted

behavior: OpenCode 2 identity rules: an owned event may omit its location but never names another session or location; a catalog model's identity is its own catalog ID, not the shared provider model ID, and a beta 'provider/id' splits into provider and ID; models compare by value, where no variant, empty and 'default' are the same and any other variant differs; a provider sign-in failure is only the exact 'provider.auth' error type.
given_when_then: Given two catalog modes sharing one provider model ID, when compared, then they are different models

behavior: The OpenCode 2 terminal stream: text and binary frames are shown and move the cursor by their UTF-8 byte length, a 0x00 meta frame sets the cursor without showing text, a malformed meta frame or empty frame is ignored, typed input goes out as text frames and close closes the socket; a socket that cannot open says 'Could not connect to the terminal' with the cause kept for Details.
given_when_then: Given a terminal socket, when frames arrive and input is typed, then output and cursor follow the frame rules

behavior: Reconnect pacing: in the foreground 1 s doubling to a 16 s cap; while the app is hidden the first two tries keep that quick pace, then each try waits a random 60 to 120 s.
given_when_then: Given repeated reconnect attempts, when the app is hidden, then after two quick tries the wait is a jittered 60-120 s

behavior: Changing a connection's project folder rebuilds the connection the same way connecting does, so an OpenCode 2, Paseo or Codex server keeps its own protocol and an isolated session still opens no network connection.
given_when_then: Given a Paseo connection, when the project folder changes, then the rebuilt connection is still Paseo

behavior: Removing OpenCode from the phone forgets every device setting of the Linux (keys under oc.linux., such as the last backup time) and nothing else: a pending reset key, drafts and other settings stay; with nothing saved it changes nothing and still succeeds.
given_when_then: Given oc.linux.* keys and oc.linuxReset.pending, when OpenCode is removed, then only the oc.linux.* keys are gone.

behavior: Attachment file cleanup keeps every payload still referenced, per owner, and removes half-written files; a write the storage refuses (no space) or one that would pass the 256 MB folder limit is reported with an actionable message before anything is published; a file system failure is a storage error whose message holds no path.
given_when_then: Given the attachment folder is at its limit, when a new attachment is saved, then it is refused with the limit message and nothing is written.

behavior: Draft attachments, stashed prompts and photo recovery each keep their files in their own folder under the app's private storage; a restart reads them back, and clearing a profile deletes that profile's files and keys in each.
given_when_then: Given a stash with an attachment, when the profile is cleared, then its attachment file and keys are gone.

behavior: A project export stopped (cancel or leaving the page) while it is still planning writes nothing; the folder picker opens once for overlapping export taps, and a picker answer after the page closed starts no export.
given_when_then: Given export planning, when cancelled or the page is closed, then no export is written

behavior: Deleting a profile waits for an in-flight Termux move-out offer dismissal and keeps new dismissals closed until its sweep ends, so the offer key is gone afterwards; a dismissal works again only after the deletion is cancelled.
given_when_then: Given a dismissal being written, when the profile is deleted, then the key is swept and cannot return

behavior: Live proof observations export only whitelisted counters, the stage and a bounded public model reference (provider up to 96 and model up to 128 safe characters), never event text, provider errors, the directory or the session ID; a bad stage, model, capability, directory, session or start is refused with a fixed error that never repeats the caller's text.
given_when_then: Given a provider error containing a secret, when a snapshot is exported, then the secret is absent

behavior: An update is never installed if its checksum does not match SHA256SUMS (the file is deleted), if its signer differs from the installed app (the detail names the signer seen), if it is another package, or if its version code is not newer.
given_when_then: Given a downloaded APK whose checksum differs, when checked, then nothing is installed, the file is deleted and the failure says checksum.

behavior: Only https downloads from this project's GitHub releases are trusted for app updates (plain http, other hosts and other repositories are refused); a test feed override is trusted only when set, and no release build or release script ever sets it.
given_when_then: Given an update URL on another host, when checked, then it is refused; given a release build, then the feed override is empty.

behavior: Linux services never follow a link: if the services folder or any folder on the way inside the Linux files is a link, saving and reading are refused and nothing is written or read outside.
given_when_then: Given the state folder is a link to another place, when the list is read, then the read is refused.

behavior: A Linux backup never holds a credential: settings files kept from home exclude SSH private keys, OpenCode, Claude and GitHub sign-in files and token or key files; projects exclude .env files, each repository's .git/config and node_modules; a setup backup leaves projects out; a setup-and-projects backup holds the package lists (apt, npm, pipx), home settings, projects and service definitions.
given_when_then: Given a home with an SSH private key and a GitHub hosts file, when backed up, then neither is in the backup while authorized_keys and .gitconfig are.

behavior: Restore reads the chosen backup and asks first (nothing runs before yes), extracts only the entries the manifest names (never paths that climb out), restores and then starts the services; a zip that is not a backup, a missing file or a newer backup is refused; a link where the restore folder goes fails the restore without writing outside or starting a job.
given_when_then: Given a backup zip with an entry ../../evil.sh, when restored, then that entry is never written.

behavior: The manage-space screen that Android opens from the system storage page ignores whatever the caller sends: extras, a target route, entry arguments and a link never reach the app, on first open and on a new intent.
given_when_then: Given a hostile intent to the manage-space screen, when it opens, then no caller extras or URL reach the app

behavior: A terminal socket that cannot connect fails with a message naming only host and port, never the ticket or other query text; a server that accepts but never upgrades is cut off by the connect timeout.
given_when_then: Given a refused or silent terminal socket, when connecting, then the error is bounded in time and ticket-free

behavior: Asking for Termux's Run commands permission (needed to move out of Termux) never crashes: an older runner falls back to the yes/no request, a refused or failed request answers denied, a cancelled dialog is denied, and only a refusal with no further asking is permanently denied.
given_when_then: Given a refused or failing permission request, when asked, then the answer is denied without an error

behavior: The loopback receiver for the Termux move-out answers a request with duplicate or invalid Authorization headers with 403 and keeps running, so the real authenticated upload still succeeds.
given_when_then: Given an unauthenticated request with two Authorization headers, when it hits the receiver, then it gets 403 and the real upload works

behavior: The app update check finds a release only when its build number is larger than the installed one; a finding survives a restart without asking again and is dropped once that build is installed; checks run at most once every 6 hours, Check now asks at once, turning the check off stops it, a failed check is retried after 30 minutes (not on every resume), and a platform that cannot install never asks.
given_when_then: Given the last check was under 6 hours ago, when the app resumes, then no new request is made; given Check now, then it asks at once.

behavior: Not now hides the update notice for that version until the next app start but keeps the badge on the gear; a newer release brings the notice back at once.
given_when_then: Given Not now on 2.2.0, when 2.2.1 is found, then the notice shows again; given no newer release, then only the gear badge stays.

behavior: A ready code-push patch says Restart to update with no gear badge, and a full release found later wins over the patch.
given_when_then: Given a ready patch and no release, when shown, then it says restart and the gear has no badge.

behavior: Update now downloads the file for this phone's ABI (arm64-v8a file for arm64, the armeabi-v7a file for a v7a-only phone, the universal file otherwise), reads SHA256SUMS (upper or lower case, star prefix allowed, junk lines ignored), skips draft releases, and shows the first sentence of the notes as the summary.
given_when_then: Given a phone that lists only armeabi-v7a, when Update now runs, then the v7a file is downloaded.

behavior: Install flow: without install permission the app opens the permission screen once and continues on return using the already checked file; cancelling a download goes back to available; cancelling Android's confirm dialog goes back to ready and Try again reuses the file; an installer failure shows Android's own words in the detail; an interrupted download resumes from the partial file with a Range request.
given_when_then: Given the confirm dialog was cancelled, when Try again, then the same file is installed without a second download.

behavior: The device check for the child-process limit reads the Android version, whether Developer options are on and whether the limit is lifted, and reports where the Developer options button opened.
given_when_then: Given Android says restrictions are off, when read, then the limit is lifted.

behavior: Heat and battery steps: a cool phone with a good battery runs at full speed; a light thermal status, a forecast of 0.7 or more, battery saver, the app out of sight, or 20% battery or less while unplugged slows the agents; a moderate status, a forecast of 0.9 or more, or 10% battery or less while unplugged also holds new work; an unknown charging state is not guessed; Always full speed turns every step off.
given_when_then: Given a forecast of 0.75 and a cool status, when decided, then agents are slowed but new work still starts.

behavior: The process budget holds new heavy agent work when the forecast is near severe or the status is moderate, still starts work on a warm phone (only slowed), and Always full speed lifts that hold while a severe pause still holds.
given_when_then: Given a forecast of 0.92, when a new agent session asks to start, then it waits as warm.

behavior: Agent background priority: on a slow step the phone agent helper is lowered (nice 10), on hold further (nice 15), going up at once; it is restored only after two calm minutes, and a hot reading in between restarts the wait; battery saver and going out of sight slow it, coming back restores after calm; Always full speed restores at once; a failed lowering is tried again and it is applied again every 5 minutes for helpers started since, not on every reading.
given_when_then: Given agents were slowed, when a cool reading comes after 30 seconds, then they stay slowed until two calm minutes pass.

behavior: The phone server start made when the app opens goes through the guarded native start: it carries its own admission token and the same restore recipe (profile and runtime) as a normal start; a Stop seen at admission withdraws it before any password is written and it is not offered as retryable; a refused start shows only plain words, never native paths or text.
given_when_then: Given the person pressed Stop just before the opening start was admitted, when the start runs, then nothing is launched and no password file is written.

behavior: The guided card for Android's child-process limit shows only on Android 14 or later with the limit in force, and only after a recent kill or frequent queuing of work: it opens Developer options when they are on, asks to turn them on when they are off or unknown, and gives instructions only when the app cannot open settings; once hidden it stays hidden until a newer kill.
given_when_then: Given the card was hidden at 10:00, when a kill happens at 11:00, then the card shows again; given the limit is lifted, then it never shows.

behavior: The priority script lowers the agent helper and all its children and nothing else, and says none when no helper runs.
given_when_then: Given a helper with a child and an unrelated process, when the script runs, then only the helper and child get the new priority.

behavior: A Linux service definition is refused with a plain problem when its name is not a short lowercase name or is reserved (server, svc, linux-job, phone-engine, agent-host, aiteam, oc-*), the name or port is already taken, the command is empty or multi-line, the folder is relative or climbs out, the stop timeout is too long, an environment name or value is invalid, the port is reserved (below 1024, above 65535, or one the app uses), or there would be more than 16 services; editing an existing one does not count against the limit.
given_when_then: Given 16 services, when a 17th is saved, then it is refused as too many; when one of them is edited, then it saves.

behavior: A service definition round-trips through its versioned text file and must name the service it is stored as (missing command or wrong name is not a definition; defaults: restart on failure, 10 s stop timeout); a state file parses only when whole; a bad definition file is left out of the list.
given_when_then: Given a half-written state file, when read, then it is ignored.

behavior: Service state shown to the person: a wanted service with the supervisor down reads as starting (not paused), with no process id; a held service reads off but on ("Paused: the phone is too hot"); a backing-off service shows its next try time; the list is one list, most urgent first (failed, port busy, retrying, running, off), then by title.
given_when_then: Given a failed and a running service, when listed, then the failed one comes first.

behavior: Service logs: marker lines are given levels (exits and give-ups as errors, backoff and busy port as warnings), the tail joins the older rotated part and drops a cut first line, and an invalid service name gives no log.
given_when_then: Given a log with an exit marker, when shown, then that line is an error.

behavior: Service actions: without the Linux every action says Linux is missing and nothing starts; Save writes the definition switched off and does not start it (an edit keeps the person's on/off choice); Start switches on, kicks the service and installs and starts the supervisor, and a second Start of a running service does nothing while Start after giving up kicks again; an unknown or path-like name is refused; stopping the last service retires the supervisor once it is off, stopping one of two keeps it; Remove waits for off then deletes the definition, choice, kick, state and log files; the list is polled only while someone watches it.
given_when_then: Given one running service, when it is stopped, then the supervisor is stopped only after the service reports off.

behavior: Keeping the service supervisor up: with nothing switched on it is not started; it starts once even if asked twice at the same time; a newer supervisor script restarts it with a keep marker so the person's choices survive (a failed restart leaves no marker); a refused start is reported as supervisor down.
given_when_then: Given a supervisor running an older script, when the app ensures it, then it restarts with the choices kept.

behavior: The heat hold for Linux services is a file the supervisor reads: critical heat holds the services (severe alone does not), they come back after two cool minutes and any heat restarts the wait; with the guard off nothing new is held but a hold left by an earlier run is given back once cool; while held, services are stopped with the person's on choice untouched and come back when the hold is removed.
given_when_then: Given a running service, when the phone reaches critical heat, then the service stops and shows as held, and starts again after two cool minutes.

behavior: The service supervisor script is valid bash, names its version, is launched by a fixed exec line, and runs a wanted service in its folder with its environment, logging a start marker.
given_when_then: Given a service with a folder and an environment value, when it starts, then its output shows that folder and value.

behavior: Supervisor restarts: a killed service comes back after a backoff (counted, exit 137 logged); three quick crashes give up and it stays down until a kick starts it again; an exit 0 with restart on failure stays exited; a kick restarts a running service.
given_when_then: Given a service that exits with 3 right away, when supervised, then it gives up after three tries and does not start again until kicked.

behavior: Stopping a service ends its whole process group and it stays stopped; a service that ignores SIGTERM is killed after its stop timeout; a removed definition is stopped and forgotten.
given_when_then: Given a service that ignores SIGTERM with a 1 s timeout, when switched off, then it is gone within a few seconds.

behavior: A service whose port is busy waits and shows port busy, then starts when the port frees; service logs are rotated at the size cap so the live file stays small.
given_when_then: Given another program holds the port, when the service is wanted, then it waits as port busy and starts after the port is released.

behavior: SIGTERM to the supervisor (the notification's Stop) stops every service and the supervisor and saves every service as off, including ones retrying, so nothing comes back when the app opens again; after the app's keep marker (a restart for a newer script) the choices are kept, the marker is used up, and the services come back.
given_when_then: Given two running services, when the notification's Stop is pressed, then both stop and stay off after the app reopens.

behavior: A backup carries a manifest (kind, time, app version, ABI, entries) that round-trips; entries with path parts are dropped; a newer format or a broken manifest is refused; file names are opencode-linux-setup[-projects]-YYYY-MM-DD.zip; restore result lines are read into counts and skipped packages; backup and restore jobs run inside the Linux job frame and lock.
given_when_then: Given a manifest with format 2, when read, then it is refused as newer.

behavior: Restore puts back missing packages (skipping ones already installed and naming ones Ubuntu no longer has), global npm and pipx tools, settings (keeping the person's changed file beside it as .before-restore), service definitions and lost projects; a project that still exists comes back beside it as "(restored)", never over it; the unpacked backup is removed; a restore with no manifest does nothing.
given_when_then: Given a project that still exists, when restored, then the backup copy appears as "app (restored)" and the current one is untouched.

behavior: The backup zip reader returns stored and deflated entries exactly as written and refuses a file that is not a zip.
given_when_then: Given a deflated entry, when extracted, then its bytes equal the original.

behavior: Back up: the saved zip has the manifest first then every part, the staging folder and temp files are cleaned and the time of the last backup is remembered; backing out of Save to saves nothing, leaves nothing and records no time; a failed job never asks where to save and leaves no parts; a failed job and a failed save are told apart, the save failure keeping its reason.
given_when_then: Given the backup job fails, when backing up, then no Save to prompt appears and no empty file is made.

behavior: A Linux job status read that began before a job started cannot end that job (a backup waiting for not running would otherwise start nothing).
given_when_then: Given a slow read started before a backup job, when it returns no job, then the job still shows as running.

behavior: Linux vitals read free phone memory from /proc/meminfo, count Linux as every process except the app (per-core CPU turned into a share of the whole phone, never above 100%, with the heaviest program named), map Android's thermal status to cool/warm/hot/too hot (unknown gives no heat), and a source that fails leaves out only its own readings.
given_when_then: Given process, memory and thermal readings, when vitals are read, then Linux share, free memory and heat are right and a failed source only blanks its own values

behavior: The vitals sentence under the Linux page states Linux memory, says nothing heats the phone only when cool, makes no heat claim without a heat reading, names a busy Linux program and its CPU when the phone is warm or hot, says the heat is not from Linux when Linux is quiet, and shows nothing with no readings.
given_when_then: Given vitals, when the sentence is built, then it says memory, heat and its cause only as far as readings allow

behavior: When Stop of the built-in Linux races a reply-work wake request that was already admitted, Stop wins: no wake lock stays held, and a process that already exited is never looked up or signalled by its reused id.
given_when_then: Given an admitted wake request, when Stop runs at the same time, then no wake lock is left and no process is signalled

behavior: An installed phone agent behind its tested pin updates itself only when nothing runs: work in progress, a running check or another setup job make it wait; one try per pin per app run; it waits when the network is not allowed, where a big download needs unmetered Wi-Fi (a phone hotspot counts as mobile data), a small one does not, and an unknown network does not block.
given_when_then: Given an agent behind its pin, when the phone is busy or on mobile data for a big download, then the update waits

behavior: An agent owes an update only when it is installed and its agent or helper version moved (not on a first check or an installation change); an agent behind the pin that still runs stays ready for work and still owes the update.
given_when_then: Given an installed agent behind its pin, when its row is built, then it is ready and owes an update

behavior: Refreshing the agent list reuses a recent sign-in answer (about 10 minutes) instead of starting the agent again; Check again always asks, and an old answer is asked again on the next refresh.
given_when_then: Given a fresh sign-in answer, when the list refreshes, then no new check starts

behavior: An automatic agent update yields to the person: while it is still downloading, new work cancels it and runs, and the update is marked to retry, not failed; once every byte is in (or progress is unknown) or it is switching versions, work waits for it instead of being refused; a check the person started still blocks work with the plain reason kept for Details.
given_when_then: Given an automatic update downloading, when the person starts work, then the work runs and the update retries later

behavior: An agent behind its pin that is still installed keeps running and is not asked for a check (with nothing left to run on, it is); an automatic update keeps the old proof until the new version passes, so a set-aside update leaves the old version qualified; a new agent version does not restart a helper already running the pinned Paseo.
given_when_then: Given an older qualified agent, when an automatic update is set aside, then the old version stays usable

behavior: For phone agents the app writes a phone note and thread caps (two build threads) into the agent's profile settings, keeps the person's own text and values (theirs win), never stacks a second block, takes back only what it added when Always full speed is chosen (leaving no files on a fresh profile), never follows a link, does nothing without a profile home, and leaves unreadable settings alone.
given_when_then: Given an agent profile, when the budget is applied twice or full speed is chosen, then only the app's own block is added or removed

behavior: New heavy work (an agent session, an AI Team run, a setup job) starts only with room under Android's 32-process limit less a reserve; with Android's limit turned off the app keeps its own ceiling (48); a hot phone (severe, or a moderate forecast near the limit) or a low battery that is not charging (20% or less) holds new work; battery is read from the kernel files; a phone it cannot read never blocks.
given_when_then: Given 25 processes or a hot phone, when an agent session asks to start, then it is held with the reason

behavior: Held work waits in a queue and starts once room frees, the phone cools or charging starts; work admitted moments ago counts before it shows in the process list; a cancelled wait ends cleanly as cancelled; waiting for room twice within an hour reads as often.
given_when_then: Given work held for room, when processes drop, then it starts; when cancelled, then it ends as cancelled

behavior: The last Android kill is the most recent SIGKILL of a Linux service in the last day that the app did not ask for; requested stops and normal exits do not count.
given_when_then: Given service exits, when the last kill is read, then only a recent unrequested SIGKILL counts

behavior: Wi-Fi share of a phone file streams a plain file inside the built-in Linux but refuses app storage (preferences, databases, app files), agent and tool settings, keys, certificates, .env and token or credential files, the app server password, and any link that leads out of the allowed area.
given_when_then: Given a chat file link to a key file or a link into app storage, when shared over Wi-Fi, then it is refused as private

behavior: A file on this phone's shared storage opens the right way: an .apk (any case) goes to the system installer, a big or binary file goes to Open with, text and anything on a remote server or inside Linux stay previews; a lookalike path such as /sdcardx is not shared storage.
given_when_then: Given a phone file path, when opened, then install, Open with or preview is chosen

behavior: The phone assistant is offered only on a 64-bit phone with enough memory (about 6 GB; a 4 GB phone or an unreadable amount is refused); a blocked phone reports why and never downloads.
given_when_then: Given a 32-bit or 4 GB phone, when the assistant is offered, then it is blocked and no download starts

behavior: The assistant model never downloads by itself; off Wi-Fi it waits and says why unless mobile data is chosen; too little free space stops it before any byte; progress is shown; cancel leaves it not installed and ready to start again; a model file of the wrong size is not counted as installed.
